q: Consider the rights-holder: 1-The general equality guarantee protects every person. 2-The six freedoms protect citizens only. 3-The protection against self-incrimination protects citizens only. Which is/are correct?
expl: The penal protections extend to every person.
why: Adjacent articles in the same Part differ on the rights-holder, which is why each must be checked separately.
trapnote: Check each article's rights-holder separately. A Part is not uniform on this question.

q: Which of the following currently states the law accurately?
options: Reservation may in no circumstances exceed one-half of the available seats
Deemed assent operates where a Governor delays a Bill beyond three months
The maximum strength of the lower House is 550
The Advisory Board in preventive detention must be convened within two months
expl: The other three describe positions that have either changed or never came into force.
why: Each wrong option was, at some point, either the law, a proposed law or a judicial position.
trapnote: Four propositions, three of them superseded or never operative. Check the date of each rule.

q: Consider provisions that bind private persons: 1-The access limb of the non-discrimination guarantee. 2-The abolition of untouchability. 3-The prohibition of forced labour. Which is/are correct?
expl: All three operate horizontally.
why: The prohibition of child labour completes the group of four provisions that reach private conduct.
trapnote: Four provisions bind private hands. These three and the prohibition of child labour.

q: On enactment versus operation: 1-The 2023 reservation amendment is enacted but not yet operative. 2-The 1978 change to the detention period was never brought into force. 3-Both are therefore of no legal effect at all. Correct?
expl: The first two are accurate; the third overstates the consequence.
why: An enacted but inoperative provision is part of the text and may become operative; it is not a nullity.
trapnote: Enacted and inoperative is a real legal state. It is not the same as never having been enacted.

q: Which pairing of institution and function is correct?
options: The State Election Commission conducts elections to panchayats and municipalities
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to panchayats and municipalities
The Finance Commission conducts elections to panchayats and municipalities
The State Finance Commission conducts elections to panchayats and municipalities
expl: Local elections rest with the State Election Commission under its own provision.
why: Institution-swap distractors are built by attaching a real function to a real but wrong body.
trapnote: Name the body and the provision together. Each of these bodies exists; only one has this function.

q: Consider: 1-The Finance Commission is a constitutional body. 2-The body that replaced the Planning Commission is an executive creation. 3-The Comptroller and Auditor General is a statutory authority. Which is/are correct?
expl: The auditor is a constitutional authority, not a statutory one.
why: Three tiers recur throughout the syllabus: constitutional, statutory and executive. Each body must be placed in one.
trapnote: Three tiers: constitutional, statutory, executive. Place every institution in exactly one.

q: A real requirement is described at the wrong stage of a process. Which of the following illustrates this?
options: Requiring a special majority for approval of a Proclamation of Emergency
Requiring the Speaker's certificate after a Money Bill is passed by the House
Requiring written Cabinet advice before a Proclamation of Emergency
Requiring an Election Commission certificate before a proclamation of President's Rule
expl: Only the Election Commission certificate belongs to extension beyond one year; certification after passage is the correct stage.
why: The remaining three describe requirements correctly placed at their own stages.
trapnote: Stage transplant: a genuine requirement moved one step earlier or later in a sequence.

q: Consider the two writ jurisdictions: 1-One is itself a Fundamental Right. 2-The other extends to legal rights beyond Part III. 3-The wider of the two is also the stronger guarantee. Which is/are correct?
expl: The wider jurisdiction is the weaker guarantee, being discretionary.
why: Scope and strength move in opposite directions between the two courts, which is counter-intuitive and therefore tested.
trapnote: Wider in scope, weaker in guarantee. The two attributes do not travel together.

q: Which statement correctly identifies a cause-and-effect pair?
options: A 2021 decision on backward-class identification was answered by a 2021 amendment
A 1973 decision on the amending power was answered by a 1971 amendment
A 2015 decision on judicial appointments was answered by a 2014 amendment
A 1994 decision on President's Rule was answered by a 1978 amendment
expl: Only the first pair runs in the correct direction, the amendment following the decision.
why: Three options reverse the chronology, which is the most frequent construction in cause-and-effect items.
trapnote: An answer must come after the thing it answers. Check the direction before the substance.

q: Consider provisions requiring ratification by half the State legislatures: 1-A change to a List in the Seventh Schedule. 2-A change to the article containing the amending power. 3-A change to the Fundamental Rights. Which is/are correct?
expl: Fundamental Rights require only a special majority.
why: The entrenched category is federal in character, which is why the rights chapter falls outside it.
trapnote: The entrenched list is federal. Rights and Directives need only a special majority.

q: On the effect of an absolute word in an option, which statement is correct?
options: Absolute words always signal a defect, no constitutional rule being without exception
Absolute words never signal a defect, the Constitution being drafted in absolute terms
Absolute words signal a defect only in questions about Fundamental Rights
Absolute words usually signal a defect, though the untouchability abolition really is absolute
expl: The heuristic is strong but not universal, and the exceptions must be known.
why: The second option converts a useful heuristic into a rule, which would produce a wrong answer on the genuine absolutes.
trapnote: A heuristic is not a rule. Learn the genuine absolutes so the heuristic does not mislead you.

q: Consider: 1-The 1976 amendment expanded the shield for laws giving effect to Directive Principles. 2-A 1980 decision cut that shield back. 3-A 2024 decision abolished the shield altogether. Which is/are correct?
expl: The 2024 decision preserved the unamended shield while narrowing a Directive Principle.
why: Narrowing a provision is not abolishing it, which is the distinction the third statement suppresses.
trapnote: Narrowing and abolishing are different outcomes. Identify which one a decision produced.

q: Which of the following is a genuine absolute in the constitutional scheme?
options: The abolition of untouchability admits no restriction and no exception
The freedom of speech admits no restriction once exercised peacefully
The right to life admits no deprivation in any circumstances whatever
The equality guarantee admits no classification of any description
expl: Untouchability is the one equality guarantee with no restriction clause.
why: Each wrong option states a right in absolute terms that the Constitution itself qualifies.
trapnote: One genuine absolute in this group. The others all carry express qualifications.

q: Consider institutions constituted by the Governor: 1-The State Election Commission. 2-The State Finance Commission. 3-The Comptroller and Auditor General. Which is/are correct?
expl: The auditor is appointed by the President.
why: Two of the three are State institutions and one is a Union constitutional authority.
trapnote: Sort by level before sorting by function. Two are State bodies and one is a Union authority.

q: On the difference between a floor and a ceiling in constitutional drafting, which statement is correct?
options: Both are floors, permitting a State to exceed them by its own legislation
Both are ceilings, prohibiting any variation above the figure prescribed
Women's reservation in panchayats is a ceiling; the employment figure is a floor
Women's reservation in panchayats is a floor; the reservation ceiling in employment is a limit
expl: One provision prescribes a minimum and the other a maximum.
why: The fourth option reverses the two, which would permit a State to reduce local reservation below one-third.
trapnote: A floor invites exceeding; a ceiling forbids it. Identify which the provision creates.

q: Consider the following as they stand today: 1-A Governor may pardon a death sentence. 2-A State legislature may restrict the rights of its police force. 3-A State legislature may prescribe punishment for untouchability. Which is/are correct?
expl: None is correct; each power belongs to a different authority.
why: All three propositions attribute a real power to the wrong authority, which is the single commonest construction in the syllabus.
trapnote: Three powers, three wrong authorities. Always read an option for its actor first.

q: Which statement about the relationship between a statute and the Constitution is correct?
options: A statute cannot abolish a constitutional guarantee, whatever its terms
A statute may abolish a constitutional guarantee if enacted by Parliament
A statute may abolish a constitutional guarantee during a Proclamation of Emergency
A statute may abolish a constitutional guarantee if placed in the Ninth Schedule
expl: Only an amendment can alter the Constitution, and even then the basic structure limits it.
why: The fourth option invokes a real protective device and overstates what it can achieve.
trapnote: A statute cannot repeal a constitutional provision. Only an amendment can, within limits.

q: Consider: 1-The special provisions for Andhra Pradesh operate through a Presidential Order. 2-The residence requirement for State posts operates through a law of Parliament. 3-Both are exercised by the same authority. Which is/are correct?
expl: Different authorities act through different instruments.
why: This pairing is the single most AP-specific distinction in the syllabus and it turns on the actor.
trapnote: President by order, Parliament by law. Two provisions, two authorities, two instruments.

q: On the treatment of a decision that has been referred to a larger bench, which statement is correct?
options: The earlier decision stands as settled law until the reference is answered
The earlier decision is suspended pending the answer to the reference
The earlier decision is overruled by the act of making the reference
The earlier decision stands, but the questions referred remain undecided
expl: A reference neither suspends nor overrules the earlier decision but leaves the questions open.
why: The second option is the closest wrong answer because it correctly says the decision stands.
trapnote: A pending reference leaves the law unsettled without displacing the existing decision.

q: Consider the following counts: 1-The national Emergency has been proclaimed three times. 2-The financial emergency has never been proclaimed. 3-No judge of the higher judiciary has ever been removed. Which is/are correct?
expl: All three are accurate.
why: Three separate counts, each of which is asked directly and each of which is often misremembered.
trapnote: Three counts worth memorising exactly: three, never, and never.
